pairs.why: Both are nearly the same toy-like wagon with the same canvas, red wheels and dirt texture, so neither is clearly closer to the smooth, soft-lit real cards.
B's canvas and wood read slightly smoother and less grainy, which is closer to the soft but not ultra-smooth finish of the real cards.
B's canvas has slightly fewer fold and weave details, which is a bit nearer the smoother real-card finish, though the two are almost identical.
Rendering, color and build are effectively the same in both, with no meaningful difference against the real cards.
A's canvas is slightly rounder and softer, while B's is a bit boxier and more textured, so A is marginally closer to the real cards' smooth volumes.
A's cover sits rounder and softer, while B's reads slightly boxy and stiff, but the difference is marginal.
A's ground and canvas are a touch less speckled and gritty, which is nearer the smoother real-card surfaces.
The two drawings are near-duplicates in shape, color, light and finish, so neither is closer to the real cards.
